newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo launches voter census for July election.
newsitem.headline: Congo launches voter census for July election.

text.p: Congo launched a voter census on Friday for presidential elections in July, with state radio and television urging everyone aged 18 and over to put down their names, witnesses said.
Friday and Saturday were declared public holidays for the census, which will last 10 days. Officials put the cost of the operation at 2.5 billion CFA francs.
Up to 10 candidates have announced plans to contest the poll. They include President Pascal Lissouba, opposition leader Bernard Kolelas, runner up in 1992 and mayor of Brazzavile.

Former Marxist military ruler Denis Sassou-Nguesso, who returned home in January after 17 months in France to an enthusiastic welcome from thousands of supporters, is widely believed to be planning to run.
He has so far made no announcement.
Sassou-Nguesso has thrown his weight behind calls for an independent national electoral commission, a demand rejected by Prime Minister Charles David Ganao.
Fighting among politically and ethnically-based militias loyal to Congo's political rivals after disputed legislative elections in 1993 killed an estimated 2,000 people in Brazzaville's suburbs.
The militias have officially disbanded but witnesses say their members remain ever present, albeit discretely.
